practice_units.title: Phases of the Moon
practice_units.problem: Explain why we see different shapes of the moon during a month.
guidance: Understand that the moon does not have its own light; it reflects sunlight.
Note that the moon revolves around the Earth.
As it moves, different parts of its illuminated surface are visible from Earth.
Identify the positions for New Moon, Half Moon, and Full Moon.
practice_units.solution: The phases of the moon occur because the amount of the moon's illuminated side that we see from Earth changes as it revolves around us.

practice_units.title: Solar and Lunar Eclipses
practice_units.problem: Identify the alignment of Earth, Moon, and Sun during a Solar Eclipse.
guidance: Recall that a Solar Eclipse happens when the Moon's shadow falls on Earth.
For this to happen, the Moon must be between the Sun and the Earth.
The three bodies must be in a straight line.
practice_units.solution: During a Solar Eclipse, the alignment is Sun - Moon - Earth.
